hints: Notice the $1.5\text{ m}$ is the distance between adjacent nodes in the stationary wave, not the wavelength of the progressive waves.
Recall that adjacent node to adjacent node is half a wavelength, so connect $1.5\text{ m}$ to $\lambda/2$.

walkthrough: Identify the given data: progressive wave frequency $f = 300\text{ Hz}$ and stationary-wave node separation $= 1.5\text{ m}$.
State the stationary-wave rule: distance between adjacent nodes $= \lambda/2$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of each superposing progressive wave.
Calculate the progressive wavelength: $\lambda/2 = 1.5\text{ m}$, so $\lambda = 2 \times 1.5 = 3.0\text{ m}$.
Apply the wave equation for a progressive wave: $v = f\lambda$.
Substitute with units: $v = 300\text{ Hz} \times 3.0\text{ m} = 900\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which checks as $\text{Hz} \times \text{m} = \text{m s}^{-1}$.
